children.text: Santacruzan is the flower procession that closes Flores de Mayo, the month-long Marian devotion of May. It recalls Saint Helena (Reyna Elena) and her search for the True Cross, and in Metro Manila the Grand Santacruzan in Intramuros is the best known.

Flores de Mayo means "flowers of May" in Spanish. It is a Philippine devotion that runs through May, the month Catholics dedicate to the Virgin Mary. Children and neighbors gather daily at the church or a neighborhood chapel to pray and offer flowers. The procession held on the last evening is the Santacruzan. The two names are often used together, but strictly speaking the month of prayer is Flores de Mayo and the procession that crowns it is the Santacruzan.

The heart of the Santacruzan is the legend of Saint Helena, mother of the Roman emperor Constantine, who went in search of the True Cross on which Jesus was crucified. Reyna Elena carries a cross and walks near the end with a boy who plays her son Constantino, and the very last place belongs to the Reyna Emperatriz, who represents Helena's title of Augusta. Earlier in the line come girls representing the titles of Mary, three women symbolizing Faith, Hope and Charity, and women playing figures from the Bible and history, all passing beneath arches decorated with flowers (arko). Some scholars trace the procession to a play called Tibag, a komedya (traditional drama) about Queen Helena's search for the cross. It is said to have been performed in Malolos, Bulacan, and its author is unknown. Over time the play turned into a walking procession in which religious and folk elements blend.

The custom is said to have arrived in Spanish colonial times, and in the Tagalog region it took hold after the 1854 proclamation of the dogma of the Immaculate Conception and the spread of a translated Marian devotional book in the late 19th century. Even within the Philippines the name and style vary by region, with terms such as sagalahan and katapusan. Today the lavish gowns and designer costumes can make it look like a beauty pageant, and in May 2026 the Archbishop of Manila urged the faithful to look beyond color and spectacle and reflect on the meaning of the cross.

For a traveler, the Santacruzan is not a show you buy a ticket for but a living event you meet on a neighborhood street. In Metro Manila the Grand Santacruzan in Intramuros is the easiest for visitors to reach, and churches, schools and barangays also hold smaller processions on evenings in late May. The dates change every year, so check announcements before you go.

This event is organized by the Intramuros Administration together with the Philippine Travel Agencies Association (PTAA), which signed a memorandum of agreement on March 25, 2025. It was reported for May 23 in 2025 and for Friday, May 22 in 2026, in the late afternoon. The procession passes against the stone buildings of the walled city, so it photographs beautifully.

Reyna Elena, who carries the cross, is the star of the procession and, depending on the community, is played by the most beautiful young woman or a respected mother. For 2026 in Intramuros, it was announced that pageant titleholder Winwyn Marquez would take the role. Constantino, who walks beside her, is usually played by a boy. The Reyna Emperatriz closes the procession, so keep that in mind when choosing where to stand.

Each reyna passes beneath, or walks beside, an arko (flower arch) decorated with flowers, fabric and local materials. Even within one procession the decorations all differ, which makes them fun to see up close.

blocks.title: Marian titles and the Ave Maria girls

children.text: In the traditional lineup, eight girls in white carry scrolls spelling A-V-E M-A-R-I-A. Figures representing the many titles of Mary follow one after another.

One procession gathers very different roles: Reyna Banderada, who stands for the homeland; Reyna Aeta and Reyna Mora, who honor indigenous and Muslim communities; and the three queens of Faith, Hope and Charity. You see many strands of Philippine history at once. In some places the dose pares (twelve pairs), led by Heneral Roldan, follow behind.

blocks.title: The feel of a neighborhood procession

children.text: The priest, altar servers and the cross lead the way while neighbors sing and pray. In a neighborhood procession you can see families and neighbors walking together, which is a different experience from a large event. The person in charge is called the hermano mayor or hermana mayor and handles the cost and preparations. How that person is chosen varies by place: a parish committee may pick, or a family may pass the role down as a vow.

blocks.title: Names and styles that differ by region

children.text: In Bicol the last day is called katapusan and combines a Mass, a Santacruzan and a procession of Mary. In Lipa, Batangas, evenings bring a devotion called luglugan. In Manila, churches, hotels and schools sometimes stage their own processions. In Pasay and Lucena, designers hold parades that showcase local craftsmanship, and in Marikina and Malabon LGBT communities hold their own Santacruzan.

items.title: Evening procession route
items.subtitle: Half a day, based in Intramuros

children.text: Check the announcement again and head to Intramuros. Parts of the route may be closed, so it is better to arrive early.
Walk around Manila Cathedral and San Agustin Church to see the preparations and flower decorations.
Pick a spot along the street. In some years the procession was reported to start in the late afternoon, so confirm the official time.
The procession passes. Take photos as the reynas go by one at a time, but do not block the way.
When it ends, have dinner near Fort Santiago or at a restaurant inside Intramuros.

The exact start time and route change every year. First check announcements from the Intramuros Administration and the event organizers. How the Intramuros event admits visitors can also change from year to year, so confirm in the announcement whether it is open and which areas it covers. Urban venues such as the Manila Hotel have also held their own santacruzan, so compare the different events.

items.title: A month of devotion
items.subtitle: Flores de Mayo at a neighborhood church

children.text: Ask locally about the May prayer time at a church or chapel near your lodging.
Quietly watch children offer flowers before the statue of Mary. Ask those nearby for permission before taking photos.
If it is late May, ask neighbors or the parish whether a barangay Santacruzan is planned.

items.title: Neighborhood procession on the last night of May
items.subtitle: Following a barangay Santacruzan on foot

children.text: Ask your lodging or a church about the time of a nearby barangay procession, then go there.
At the starting point, watch the priest, altar servers and cross lead off, and see the flowers placed along both sides of the street.
From a distance, watch the shared snack gathering at the hermano mayor's home or the church yard. If you are not invited, simply give a polite greeting.
Barangay processions are often not publicly announced, so if watching is your goal, prefer open events such as the one in Intramuros.
From Ninoy Aquino International Airport to Intramuros, a Grab taxi usually takes about
30–60 minutes
, and longer at rush hour.
On event day the roads inside and around the walls may be closed, so it is better to walk in from an entrance outside the walls (for example near Puerto Real).
The procession route may change from year to year, so check the organizers' announcements.
From LRT-1 Central Terminal or the Padre Burgos side, you can walk or take a short ride to Intramuros. Check the latest announcements for routes and operating hours.
Barangay processions are scattered, so use Grab or a jeepney, and arrange a taxi in advance for the late ride home.
Flores de Mayo lasts all through May, but the best sight is the Santacruzan procession on a late-May evening. The Intramuros event fell on May 23, 2025 and May 22, 2026, both Fridays in late May.
Late May is hot and humid at the end of the dry season, with strong afternoon sun and the chance of a shower. Even if the procession starts in the late afternoon, pack light clothing and an umbrella.
Note that the Marian procession of Manila Cathedral is a separate event held in Plaza de Roma on the first Sunday of December, not in May. Do not confuse it with the May Santacruzan.

There are few hotels inside Intramuros, so many travelers stay in central Manila (Ermita, Malate) or Makati and travel in. The procession ends in the evening, so decide your ride in advance.
You can have Filipino meals at restaurants and cafés inside the walls. They get crowded on event day, so check whether reservations are needed. Check prices at each place locally.

After the procession, many travelers go on to eat around the plaza near Fort Santiago or in the dining area of Malate. Roads are congested on event evenings, so eat early before the procession or leave yourself time afterward. Korean travelers will find it convenient to stay in Ermita or Malate.
The date and route change every year, so check announcements from the Intramuros Administration and PTAA before you leave.
The procession is a religious event, so be quiet and respectful when the cross or the statue of Mary passes.
Follow organizers' guidance on camera flash and drones, and do not block a reyna's path.
May is hot. Bring a hat, water and a compact umbrella.
Locals know small barangay processions best. Ask your hotel staff or a church.
Dress neatly. Inside churches, clothing covering shoulders and knees is the safe choice.
The dates in this guide are based on 2025–2026 reports, so always check the latest announcements for the next year's schedule.
Children along the road sometimes toss petals as the reynas and arkos pass. Enjoy the atmosphere, but look around before joining in.
Events, routes and road closures change every year, so check the official announcement right before your visit.
Traffic may be controlled along the procession route, which slows vehicles.
Watch for pickpockets in the crowd and carry your bag in front.
When returning late in the evening, arrange a taxi in advance.
A waterproof bag or raincoat helps in case of a shower.
Ask permission before taking close-up photos of people.
